tei:div.tei:p: The Prayer of Moses the man of God: Lord, Thou hast been a dwelling for us in every generation. Before the mountains were born and Thou didst bring forth the earth and the world, from eternity to eternity Thou art God. Thou dost restore mortals to contrition and say: Return, children of men. For a thousand years are in Thine eyes as a yesterday that passes and as a watch in the night. Thou hast carried them off: they are in sleep; in the morning he is renewed like grass. In the morning it blossoms and is renewed, in the evening it withers and dries. For we are consumed through Thine anger and terrified through Thy wrath. Thou hast placed our sins before Thee, our secret transgressions before the light of Thy countenance. For all our days pass away through Thine anger, we end our years like a fleeting thought. The days of our years — they are seventy years or, at full strength, eighty years, and their pride is toil and sorrow, since swiftly severed do we fly away. Who knows the might of Thine anger and is Thy wrath according to the fear of Thee? To count our days teach us well so that we may acquire a wise heart. Turn again, O Lord — how much longer — and take pity on Thy servants. Satisfy us in the morning with Thy grace that we may exult and rejoice all our days. Cause us to rejoice as long as the days when Thou didst afflict us and the years when we saw misfortune. Let Thy work become apparent to Thy servants, and Thy splendour to their children; and may the favour of the Lord our God be upon us; and firmly establish the work of our hands for us, the work of our hands, establish it firmly.
